clue.text: One dreads having a case of the jitters

blocks.note: first meaning: a person full of fear and anxiety
second meaning, read literally: a case is a package and jitters are nerves

explanation.surface: Someone frets about coming down with a fit of the jitters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One dreads' reads as a person who dreads things; the second half is the phrase taken literally, a package (case) of nerves (jitters).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person who is extremely anxious and on edge, and literally names a parcel of nerve fibres.

clue.text: Keynotes Kent hit differently in this novelty piano solo

indicators.note: arranged differently tells us the preceding words are to be put in another order

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A pianist strikes keynotes in an unusual way in a light-hearted piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitten on the Keys is a 1921 ragtime novelty piece by Zez Confrey; the surface even hints at it through keynotes struck.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a famous comic ragtime composition for solo pianist, imitating a cat walking across a keyboard.

clue.text: Travellers’ train set in motion

indicators.note: letters put in motion are stirred about and come to rest in a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A model railway belonging to some wanderers gets switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train set' looks like a toy, and 'set in motion' like a phrase, but 'in' belongs to the letters and only 'motion' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerants are people who move from place to place without a fixed home, such as wandering workers.

clue.text: Progress made on top road

blocks.note: the head is the top of something
a way is a road or path

explanation.surface: Advancement achieved while travelling along a high road.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the top piece above the road piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To make headway is to advance or move forward, so the noun names forward movement.

clue.text: Security for the Italian undergraduate

blocks.note: a student working towards a Bachelor of Arts degree
il is Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: Some guarantee being demanded on behalf of a student from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in the reverse of clue order: the degree first, then the Italian article.
explanation.definitionFit: Bail is money pledged to a court to secure an accused person's release before trial.

clue.text: Mystery surrounding Atlantic island takes shape

blocks.note: a British island territory in the North Atlantic
a three-sided shape

explanation.surface: An enigma around an ocean isle slowly begins to form.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bermuda Triangle is the stretch of ocean around Bermuda where ships and planes are said to vanish mysteriously.
explanation.definitionFit: The region is famous as an unexplained puzzle, legendary for disappearances of vessels and aircraft.

clue.text: Efficiency personified in tanned gardener

blocks.note: capability is competence or efficiency
skin that is tanned is brown

explanation.surface: A sunburnt groundsman is the very embodiment of effectiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown was the great 18th-century English landscape designer, nicknamed for saying grounds had capability.
explanation.definitionFit: He laid out the parkland of many English country estates, the most famous landscape designer in Britain.

clue.text: Beth's in a muddle, having a drink

indicators.note: in a muddle means jumbled up and out of order

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Beth is confused, perhaps because she has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'a' is part of the letters to shuffle; the second goes with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit flavoured with wormwood.

clue.text: Silver, for example, apparently causing disparity between young and old?

blocks.note: surface reading: silver hair, say, seemingly marks out the older party
setter's reading: Ag is the symbol for silver and e.g. means for example, so the letters themselves seem to spell the phrase

explanation.surface: Grey hair seems to be what separates the generations.
explanation.walkthrough: Ag (silver) plus e.g. (for example) appear to start AGE GAP, hence 'apparently'; silver hair is also a visible sign of age.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the difference in years between two people, especially a couple or generations.

clue.text: A heavyweight takes on school

blocks.note: taken as written
Eton is a famous English private school

explanation.surface: A burly fighter picks a fight with a whole school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A heavyweight' reads as a boxer but is the definition: something weighing a ton.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weighing a full imperial ton is very heavy indeed, the ultimate massive object.

clue.text: Lid’s replaced: Jane Austen’s heroine has problems

indicators.note: letters that are replaced are put back in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Emma is the title heroine of an Austen novel, with the possessive s kept

explanation.surface: An Austen character is troubled once a lid has been put back.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilemmas are awkward situations requiring a choice between unwelcome alternatives, so difficulties or quandaries.

clue.text: Exceptional luck — all new leading characters have style

indicators.note: the leading characters of words are the ones at their front, so only initials count

blocks.note: initials of these four words

explanation.surface: Fresh stars, blessed with remarkable fortune, have flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash and flair, a stylish energy and verve in how something is done.

clue.text: Red admiral battered the Spanish side

indicators.note: something battered is knocked out of its original shape

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A butterfly, or a Communist naval officer, gets beaten up by the Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: A red admiral is a butterfly; 'side' means a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: Real Madrid is the celebrated football club from Spain's capital, a team or side.

clue.text: Runners carry me to new distance recorders

indicators.note: made new means formed afresh, so the letters are rearranged
to carry something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: milers are athletes who race over a mile
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Athletes bring a new person along to some measuring devices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests competitors or plants; here they are milers, who hold the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Milometers are the instruments in a car that log how many miles have been travelled.

clue.text: Making money by creating new words

blocks.note: first meaning: stamping metal into currency
second meaning: inventing a fresh term or phrase

explanation.surface: Earning cash through inventing vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin is literally to mint currency and figuratively to invent an expression, both forms of minting.

clue.text: Unfortunately, silt got into part of vocal apparatus

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement is a bad one, so the letters must be redone

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Mud has sadly got into someone's throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The glottis is the opening between the vocal cords in the larynx, a component of speech production.

clue.text: A ransom organised for rower

indicators.note: organised means arranged into order, so the letters take a new arrangement

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Kidnappers arrange a payout for the return of a rower.
explanation.definitionFit: An oarsman is a person who propels a boat with oars, especially in a racing crew.

clue.text: Zest for excitement

blocks.note: first meaning: keen eagerness
second meaning: passionate interest and fervour

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single phrase, eagerness to be excited, but the two nouns are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiasm is intense enjoyment and eager interest, matching both gusto and keen excitement.

clue.text: Subsidy lady gets, partly for romantic poem

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the words is used, so the answer sits inside them

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A woman receives a grant for writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: IDYL is the American spelling of idyll.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short poem describing an idealised pastoral or romantic scene of rustic life.

clue.text: Kirk tees off, with devotees of a TV series

indicators.note: things that go off are spoiled or knocked awry, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Captain Kirk starts a round of golf among his fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tees off' looks like golf, but 'off' alone signals the shuffle; Kirk is the Star Trek captain, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Trekkies are the passionate fans of the science-fiction programme Star Trek.

clue.text: One finds no sodium under here off the Scottish coast

blocks.note: Roman numeral for one
O is zero, nothing
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: Someone discovers there is no salt in this place off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'under' places the sodium symbol below the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, off the west of Scotland, famed for its abbey.

clue.text: Singers with a number of alternatives?

blocks.note: ten is a number
the word 'or' introduces an alternative, so several of them

explanation.surface: Vocalists who have plenty of options.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of 'alternatives' as instances of the word 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenors are male vocalists with the highest ordinary adult male voice range.

clue.text: Trust with confidence about student over there

blocks.note: re means concerning
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
yon is an old word for that distant place

explanation.surface: A confident belief concerning a learner who is far away.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on someone is to have faith that they will come through, believing firmly in them.

clue.text: Passion flower opens out, surprisingly, in draughts

indicators.note: the word before it is taken out, removed from the longer phrase
a surprising arrangement is an unexpected one, so the remaining letters are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
these letters are removed from the plant's name

explanation.surface: A climbing plant unexpectedly blooms in a breezy spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opens out' looks like a flower blooming, but 'opens' is the letters removed and 'out' the instruction to remove them.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughts are currents of cool air moving through a room, which are flows of air.
